name: Émile Duclaux
bio: French microbiologist and chemist, a student of Pasteur and his successor at the Institut Pasteur, and Mary Robinson's second husband. She married him in 1902, eight years after Darmesteter's death, and was widowed again in 1904. She lived on among his children, took his name, and died at Aurillac in 1944.
bio_note: THE MARRIAGE YEAR IS IN CONFLICT AND IS NOT RESOLVED: Wikipedia says 1902, Wikidata's P580 qualifier says 1901, and NEITHER CARRIES A REFERENCE. 1902 is entered because it is the fuller of the two statements and sits in continuous prose, but a later pass should settle it from the ODNB entry for Mary Duclaux or from Patricia Rigg's Blackwell encyclopedia article.
